verification_method: Independent direct OpenCascade BRepAlgoAPI_Common on the exported STEP solids at the actual submitted assembly.json translations (all rotations zero). All 12 base seats, all neighbouring pairs, sampled vertical withdrawal, the submitted stacked pose plus a generic stacking matrix, label text geometry, finger probes, long-screw gauges and free-volume capacity. Label sightlines are ray casts on the exported STLs (sightlines.py, trimesh). Design generator and the submission verify.py were never executed.

withdrawal.note: stacked bin must be lifted first; host then lifts clear

font_review.embedded_ttf_description: Two-bead FDM font: every stroke is exactly two extrusion widths (w). Fusion text Height = 14 x line width (cap height); em = 20 x line width.
font_review.note: The README recommends a 0.4 mm nozzle. At em = 20 w the 4.6-6.5 mm em labels need 0.23-0.33 mm extrusion lines, below the font description target of 8 mm em at 0.4 mm lines. Readability at these sizes is a slicer/print question that remains untested.

capacity_estimate.method: Direct OCP free volume inside each compartment rectangle from the 6.0 mm floor to the label-shelf top (nom_h - 2 mm); scoop, shelf and gusset solid subtracted. Solid nominal ISO hardware, 60% packing assumed, same convention as the earlier gemini-gridfinity review. Geometry only, no loading test.

label_sightlines.method: trimesh ray casts from up to 60 sampled raised-text top facets per label toward -Y at the listed elevations and yaw; a label counts as readable at an elevation when >= 95% of its rays clear all parts.

limitations: Rigid exported-geometry checks; no print, slice, printer tolerance, elephant foot, friction or filled-bin handling.
Withdrawal, stacking release and sightlines are discrete samples, not continuous motion or visibility proofs.
Capacity is free volume times an assumed 60% packing fraction; no hardware was loaded and tiny-part pickup was not tried.
Probe positions use the submission parameters; text cap heights are measured from the exported solid.
Bench viewing positions are modelled as rays toward -Y (the M4 front row) with +/-30 degree yaw; eye height and distance are not modelled.
